newsitem.title: TAJIKISTAN: Tajik government seals truce with rebels.
newsitem.headline: Tajik government seals truce with rebels.

text.p: A ceasefire between the Tajik government and Islamic opposition came into effect on Tuesday to end fighting which broke out after the rebels seized two towns in north-central Tajikistan this month.

The deal, signed late on Monday, involves stopping all military activity in the region, removing all checkpoints along the road to the Karategin valley from the capital Dushanbe and reinstating local authorities in the two captured towns.
It also allows the resumption of passenger traffic and the transport of humanitarian aid to the region.

It was signed in the central town of Garm by Amircul Azimov from the government and field commander Mirzokhudga Nazimov with Khasan Abaza on behalf of the United Nations mission which is monitoring an existing but much violated nationwide ceasefire.
"This protocol is temporary and is valid until the political issues are settled during the next stage of talks," said Dzhomalladdin Makhmudov, co-chairman of the united opposition.
The date of the next round of talks has not yet been fixed.

The deal did not appear to include the total withdrawal of government troops from the region which had been demanded by the rebels, and opposition commanders refused a government demand to retreat to positions they held before the September 6 attack.

Officials at the Tajik defence ministry and U.N. observers said on Monday the opposition fully controlled Tajikabad, 245 km (150 miles) northeast of Dushanbe, after letting a last besieged unit of government troops withdraw from the town's airport.
On September 6, the opposition seized Dzhirgatal, some 35 km (20 miles), further to the northeast.

The rebels, who have waged a guerrilla war against the Dushanbe authorities since their defeat in a 1992 civil war, said they were responding to the government seizure of the strategic town of Tavildara.

Tavildara, 200 km (120 miles) east of Dushanbe, controls the narrow neck of mountainous country that links the western and eastern halves of Tajikistan. It fell to the government after weeks of fighting. Tajikabad and Dzhirgatal lie in the northern part of this central neck.
The U.N. has condemned the rebel seizure of Dzhirgatal a breach of a September 1994 ceasefire, which was extended in July, and called on both sides to retreat to previously held positions.
Tens of thousands have died and many more have lost their homes in fighting which devastated the country after the former Soviet republic gained independence on September 9, 1991.
